hair: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent modular HAIR sprite atlas for a faithful private remake of Baseball Heroes, matching the supplied original reference images. The first image is the game's original character artwork and the second is its original character-making UI: use these only as style/hairstyle references. Create ONE atlas of eight ISOLATED HAIRSTYLES ONLY, arranged in a precise 4-column x 2-row evenly spaced grid on genuine transparent background. Every cell contains a single wig/hair silhouette with black confident curved comic outlines and two simple flat cel shades, the same scale and front/very slight three-quarter view. Do NOT include heads, faces, eyes, necks, bodies, helmets, labels or backgrounds. Keep the forehead/face opening transparent. Use uniform purple material (#694392 base, lighter violet cel highlight) on all wigs so the game can recolor them; preserve black outlines. Hair shapes in row-major order: 1 Shaggy blond-style long pointed locks/fringe from screenshot; 2 Devilock rounded straight draping side-part long bangs; 3 Volume layered swept voluminous side bangs as the blue hero in screenshot; 4 Slicked-Back swept backwards, part at forehead and two short temple locks; 5 Crew Cut very short close cropped crown with a broad curved hairline; 6 Cornrows tightly braided rows arranged from forehead towards back with detailed small interwoven strands; 7 Messy soft tousled outward curved locks; 8 Slick side part with wide smooth swoop crossing forehead. Match the original 2D Flash art, bold black ink, clean curving silhouettes, simple angular cel shadows. All eight complete silhouettes must fit their own cell with ample transparent padding, no touching neighboring cells and no cropping. No pixel art, 3D, textures, gradients, glow, watermark or text.
body: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: modular transparent BASEBALL BODY animation sprite atlas. Use the first supplied image (original Baseball Heroes characters) as the art-style reference, the second original creation screen as the standing pose and proportions reference, and the third atlas only as an action-sequence reference. Generate ONE precise 4-column by 5-row atlas of TWENTY HEADLESS baseball-player bodies, all complete and isolated with genuine transparent background and generous separation. Do not draw heads, hair, eyes, faces, helmets or neck-sized placeholder circles: end each body at a short skin-colored neck stump and white shirt collar so a customizable head can be attached at runtime. Body proportion in the original game is short torso, short legs, big shoes, compact youthful chibi silhouette. Not adult realistic anatomy. Confident thick black ink, clean flat cel colors with one angular shadow, no gradients, no 3D rendering, no shading textures, no text or numbers or logos. All wear a WHITE baseball jersey with RED accent sleeves/vertical stripe, white pants, charcoal belt and shoes with white sole, pale peach skin, white batting gloves, tan wooden bat. Keep each figure at matching scale, feet at the same vertical baseline inside its own cell, neck stump centered near its cell's center. Do not let bat extend outside its cell. Each body should be approximately 140 pixels high when viewed at native game scale. FOUR standing FRONT VIEW poses in first row: neutral standing holding bat resting over right shoulder (as creation reference), subtle breathing same pose, friendly small nod same pose, pleased energetic pose with bat over shoulder. Rows 2-5: sixteen baseball batting poses, THREE QUARTER REAR VIEW facing right toward pitcher, like action atlas but original flat graphic style. In row-major order these sixteen are: ready stance, ready slight weight shift, loading weight onto back foot, front knee raised, stride forward; start swing, exact horizontal bat contact to right, high follow through, torso rotating follow through, finished backswing behind left shoulder, bat lowered recovering, back to ready stance; disappointed headless shoulder slump with lowered bat, returning to ready, bat raised celebratory success, relaxed success stance. Bold curves and black strokes, no motion trails, no ground shadows, no ball, no scenery, no labels or grids. Respect twenty isolated cells, consistent equipment, complete shoes/hands/bat, transparent top region reserved for the customizable heads.
